questions.q: What's the difference between a customer and a guest?
questions.a: A customer buys once, while a guest has a relationship with your brand and keeps coming back. Treating people as guests means recognizing them, remembering what they like and making them feel welcome every time. That repeat behavior compounds into a large share of your revenue.

questions.q: Why do repeat guests matter so much for restaurant growth?
questions.a: Repeat guests are where growth compounds, because each return visit builds on the last. A relatively small group of loyal guests often drives most of a brand's revenue. When you improve the guest experience, satisfaction, repeat visits and sales tend to rise together.

questions.q: Why is it hard for multi-location brands to turn customers into guests?
questions.a: Most brands run customer service, operations and marketing on separate tools, so the guest experience is disconnected. Teams end up reacting to problems, and chances to build loyalty slip through the gaps between them. Without a unified view, it's hard to track the full repeat-guest lifecycle, let alone improve it.

questions.q: How can a restaurant brand turn more first-time customers into regulars?
questions.a: Respond to guests quickly on every channel, recover unhappy guests with timely offers and fix the recurring issues behind complaints at each store. Then use what you know about each guest to send relevant offers that bring them back. Doing all of this from one connected system makes it easier to keep going as you add locations.
